ask: Make a 2-week campaign from our blog post acme.com/blog/pricing-guide and the customer quotes in our Google Doc. LinkedIn only.
before: The plan was shown and got a yes: Pricing guide, Product Education (teach one thing about how it works), Nov 16 to Nov 29, 2 images and 2 carousels a week, 8 drafts to review, Bolta writes it.

arguments.name: Pricing guide
arguments.theme: How to price agency retainers, from our pricing guide

steps.why: A guide that teaches is Product Education. No mix: Content defaults or the strategy's 2 images and 2 carousels, which LinkedIn takes. The link is the one the user gave.

arguments.context_notes: Built from the pricing guide. Customer quotes come from the brand's own document; quote only what it says.

steps.why: The blog post is a url source. A Google Doc can't be added by a call: a file source takes only an id the campaign already shows. So the user attaches it on the campaign page (Context, upload), or pastes the quotes for the notes.
A new source is pending and the writer ignores it until read. The page is read in this call: ready, or failed with an error to say as given.
After the user said they attached the doc: its file row now shows in context_sources with an id, still pending.
A file stays pending until Bolta has read it; if it still says pending, analyze it again later. Start only once both rows are ready, or the user accepts going without the quotes.

say: Bolta read the pricing guide and your quotes doc for Acme's Pricing guide campaign: Nov 16 to Nov 29 on LinkedIn, 8 drafts to review. Start it?
never: Saying a source was read before its row reads ready.
Using a link found inside the blog post as the call-to-action link.
Starting it while the doc the user cared about is still unread, without saying so.
